detector.name: mechanical lane-disjointness detector (path/ownership-overlap)
detector.implementation: check_lane_disjointness in tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app (owned Rust, zero third-party deps), driven through the retirement-marked bridge bin command check-disjoint; contract at specs/fabric-drive-loop-state.json#lane_disjointness
detector.decision_rule: Path overlap (equal or component-wise directory-prefix paths across lanes) verdicts overlap-serialize-to-integrator; zero overlaps verdict disjoint; lane count is capped fail-closed by independent reviewer capacity (2 lanes <= 2 independent reviewers this run); malformed surfaces are refused fail-closed. Not judgment: the detector decided what ran concurrently, pre-flight over the DECLARED surfaces and post-run over the ACTUAL touched paths.

lane_fabric_f_round_1.rationale_highlights: Reviewer traced the require_regular_file admission truth-table by hand (regular file / symlink-to-file / symlink-to-dir / dangling symlink / directory / fifo-socket) and verified the DirEntry::file_type no-follow vs fs::metadata follow split, including TOCTOU reasoning (d_type from the readdir buffer reflects enumeration-time truth; DT_UNKNOWN fallback surfaces as environmental Io; symlink target deleted mid-race IS the dangling case). Placement verified: exactly one fs::read_dir in the crate, both listing callers route through list_json_ids with no bypass; tmp carve-out untouched. Pre-change failure of BOTH regression tests traced and empirically grounded on this darwin host (read_to_string on a directory yields IsADirectory Io -> pre-fix Corrupt match fails; dangling symlink yields NotFound -> pre-fix silent drop returns Ok). No false closure: valid-symlink target planted outside the listed dir. cfg(unix) scope verified compile-portable. Independence verified: the diff references none of main.rs's new symbols. Reviewer independently ran cargo test (46/46) and clippy (clean).
